Article Title: Xi in the room, PM Modi warns against 'weaponisation of critical minerals'
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday warned against the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals, saying that there is a need for inclusivity in the adoption of technology.During his closing remarks on the second day of the Brics summit, PM Modi said that tightening control over technology and critical minerals could hinder shared progress of countries."Under the umbrella of innovation, the Brics Incubator Network will connect our startups and incubators. We have proposed the Brics Startup Innovation Fund to promote innovative and scalable solutions. The Brics Network on Digital Agriculture will create new opportunities for farmers; through this initiative, AI, geospatial technology, and digital public infrastructure will be aligned with the actual needs of farmers. The weaponisation of technology and critical minerals could hinder our shared progress; therefore, we have emphasised inclusivity in the adoption of technology,” PM Modi said.“The strength of Brics lies in our diversity and cooperation. We may be rooted in different realities, but together we rise through cooperation and blossom for humanity. May our diversity remain our identity, our cooperation serve as our inspiration, and our progress benefit all of humanity," he added.Interestingly, the remarks were made in the presence of Chinese President Xi Jinping. Although the Prime Minister did not name any particular country, the remarks can be seen as a message to Beijing, which holds a dominant position in global supply chains for critical minerals and rare earths.Last year, China tightened its export controls on rare earths and other materials critical for advanced tech manufacturing during trade negotiations with the United States.China controls more than 90 percent of global rare-earth refining, giving it enormous leverage over critical technologies, from the permanent magnets used in EVs and AI data centres to components in advanced electronics and semiconductors.During his address, PM Modi also said that “India has advanced the spirit of friendship, partnership, and cooperation through the Brics platform.”“We have endeavoured to ensure that Brics cooperation is not limited to governments alone; we want our entrepreneurs, farmers, researchers, women, youth, and ordinary citizens to become active participants as well,” PM Modi said."I can say from personal experience that the trust of Global South nations in Brics has grown, because their voices are heard, their experiences are respected, and solutions are crafted not just for them, but with them. The strength of Brics lies in our diversity and cooperation. We may be rooted in different realities, but together we rise through cooperation and blossom for humanity. May our diversity remain our identity, our cooperation serve as our inspiration, and our progress benefit all of humanity," he added.The last leg of the summit focused on the core pillars of India's 2026 Brics chairship -- resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. The two-day summit is being hosted by India on September 12-13 under the chairship theme, “Building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability."The open session is part of the two-day Brics summit being hosted by India on September 12-13 under the chairship theme, “Building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability."
Article Summary: Pm modi warns against the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals. Remarks were made in the presence of chinese president xi jinping. Last year, china tightened its export controls on rare earths and other materials critical for advanced tech manufacturing during trade negotiations with the united states.

Stronger India-China ties are strategically important for the two countries and the wider Global South, a Chinese journalist said on Sunday, a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping reaffirmed their commitment to stabilising bilateral relations on the sidelines of the Brics summit in New Delhi.Speaking to news agency ANI, Qingduo U, a journalist with Chinese state broadcaster CGTN, said the size of India and China’s populations and economies made their relationship one of the world’s most consequential.“China and India probably have the most consequential relationship in the world, as well as in BRICS,” he said, stressing that both countries needed to stabilise their ties and take a long-term view of the relationship.He welcomed the Brics push for a more representative global order, saying the rise of the Global South made greater representation in institutions such as the United Nations Security Council, International Monetary Fund and World Bank a “reasonable demand”.“Multipolarity, or multipolar development, is here. It’s irreversible. There’s a rise of the Global South, which is unstoppable. That’s the reality,” he said, calling for reforms to make the global order “more balanced, more representative, and more just”.On the PM Modi-Xi meeting, Qingduo said the two leaders had demonstrated a “strategic vision and long-term perspective” by stressing peace and tranquillity along the India-China border.PM Modi and President Xi on Saturday expressed commitment to a “fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable” resolution of the boundary question and agreed that bilateral ties should be viewed from a strategic and long-term perspective. PM Modi said differences between the two countries should not become disputes and that the relationship should be guided by mutual respect, sensitivity and interest, according to the ministry of external affairs.Meanwhile, Gaziza Uzak, head of Kazakhstan’s NazarMedia and a member of the country’s Union of Journalists, praised India’s leadership of the Brics summit and said the gathering offered countries an opportunity to strengthen cooperation.“We support Modi’s programme because I think he speaks more good and best information for us to save our planet and to make our lives and our relationships better,” she said.Nigerian journalist Emperor Simon of Channels Television also described the summit as an important forum for Brics members and partner countries to discuss global challenges and future cooperation.The two-day summit is being hosted by India on September 12-13 under the chairship theme, “Building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability."

Qingduo u, a journalist with chinese state broadcaster cgtn, said the size of india and china’s populations and economies made their relationship one of the world's most consequential.

NEW DELHI: Chinese President Xi Jinping skipped a gala dinner hosted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for Brics leaders and other dignitaries on Saturday, after attending the first day of the summit and holding a bilateral meeting with PM Modi.Sources aware of the matter told news agency PTI that Xi was absent from the dinner at Bharat Mandapam, where Russian President Vladimir Putin and other Brics leaders were present. NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi joined Russian President Vladimir Putin , Chinese President Xi Jinping and other world leaders for a family photo at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on Sunday as the 18th Brics Summit entered its second and final day.PM Modi welcomed several visiting leaders at the summit venue, including Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, Burundi President Evariste Ndayishimiye, Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Uganda Vice President Jessica Alupo.The leaders gathered for the family photo ahead of an open session focused on resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability — the core pillars of India's theme for the summit.The session, titled ‘Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth’, is being held at the Summit Hall inside Bharat Mandapam. Article Title: Three years before 9/11, CIA warned Clinton that Bin Laden wanted to strike India
Article Text:
Osama bin Laden (File photo)

Three years before the 9/11 attacks shocked the United States, then-President Bill Clinton was warned by the CIA that Osama bin Laden intended to carry out attacks in India, Pakistan, Uganda and possibly Nigeria.A newly declassified CIA warning dated August 28, 1998, said Bin Laden had survived US missile strikes in Afghanistan and retained a network of individuals and allied groups across at least 60 countries that could be used to mount attacks.The assessment specifically listed India and Pakistan, along with Egypt, the Arabian Peninsula – particularly Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Yemen – Uganda and possibly Nigeria, as countries where Bin Laden intended to conduct attacks.Bin Laden also viewed India as part of what he described as a “Crusader-Zionist-Hindu” conspiracy against the Islamic world, reflecting the ideological lens through which he framed India and its relationship with the US and Israel.The CIA said Bin Laden was also considering further attacks against the US and UK, although he had not indicated precise targets or timing.The assessment came weeks after the August 1998 bombings of US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania, which killed more than 200 people and brought Bin Laden's organisation firmly into the sights of US counterterrorism agencies.The newly released document said Bin Laden’s infrastructure in North America, Europe and East Asia also lent credibility to reports that he could target US interests in those regions.The CIA assessment further noted that Bin Laden had authorised an associate to explore attacks in the US and that US officials had recently helped arrest Bin Laden operatives preparing attacks in Tirana and possibly Baku.The India reference is significant because it shows that the threat posed by Bin Laden’s network was being assessed as extending beyond the Middle East, Africa and the US well before the September 11 attacks.The August 1998 assessment was part of a series of intelligence warnings about Bin Laden that accumulated in the years before 9/11. The newly released material includes warnings about his pursuit of unconventional weapons, potential attacks on US soil and, later, the possibility of aircraft hijackings.The documents also show that Bin Laden’s network was not viewed as a purely Afghanistan-based threat. The CIA described a global infrastructure capable of supporting or inspiring attacks across multiple regions.For India, the 1998 assessment offers an early glimpse of how New Delhi had already figured in US intelligence assessments of the emerging Bin Laden threat, years before the attacks that would transform global counterterrorism policy.
Article Summary: Bin laden viewed india as part of what he described as a “crusader-zionist-hindu” conspiracy against the islamic world. The august 1998 assessment was part of a series of intelligence warnings about bin laden that accumulated in the years before 9/11.

China Southern Airlines will restart regular passenger flights between Guangzhou and New Delhi from September 21, the Global Times reported on Saturday.The announcement came ahead of Chinese president Xi Jinping’s visit to India for the Brics summit. The airline said the resumption would take its total operations across eight round-trip routes in South Asia to more than 100 flights a week. The Guangzhou-New Delhi service had been suspended for six years.Air connectivity between India and China has gradually improved in recent months.Air China resumed its Beijing-Delhi service in April, while China Eastern Airlines restarted direct flights between Kunming and Kolkata on April 18.Indian carrier IndiGo also launched a daily non-stop service between Kolkata and Shanghai on March 30. The airline had earlier restored flights from Kolkata to Guangzhou and later began operating from Delhi to the Chinese city.The resumption of direct flights followed confirmation from India’s ministry of external affairs. Air links between the two countries had been suspended during the Covid-19 pandemic and amid tensions following the Doklam and Galwan standoffs.Xi left Beijing on Saturday for the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi at Modi’s invitation, China’s state news agency Xinhua reported.The Chinese president is scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi later in the day.Xi’s delegation includes Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China and director of its General Office, and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.According to Xinhua, Xi is expected to advance proposals on cooperation among Global South countries, building on his remarks at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek.Brics has become a major platform for emerging economies to coordinate on trade, finance, technology, development and global governance. The grouping also seeks to promote greater cooperation among countries of the Global South.

Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Summit , beginning a two-day visit to India that marks his first trip to the country in seven years.Xi was received at the Delhi airport by Union minister of state for commerce and industry Jitin Prasada, with cultural artistes from the Northeast and other parts of India performing traditional dances to welcome the Chinese leader. The discussions covered the India-China boundary question, including delimitation of the frontier, trans-boundary cooperation and maintaining peace along the LAC.Both Doval and Wang are designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism, established in 2003 to address the 3,488-km India-China border dispute. Article Title: 'Prioritise national interest': Shashi Tharoor advises govt to keep Brics 'non-West'

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday cautioned that the Brics summit hosted by India should not appear to be an anti-West platform, as that would not be in sync with the country’s national interests.Tharoor, who served as a diplomat at the United Nations for decades, advised the government to showcase the concerns of the Global South while keeping India’s direct national interests in mind."As chair, we have a particular responsibility to showcase both the Brics as a forum, the concerns of the Global South in general, but also while bearing very, very carefully in mind our direct national interests. We want Brics to be a forum that is non-West, but not anti-West. That is exactly actually the same agenda as every other country. There are some others in Brics who are very happy to take it as a geopolitical non-Western, but also anti-Western platform," Tharoor told news agency PTI.He also said that PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"."And I would like to say that that would not be in India's national interest...Becauseall these world leaders are in India, there will be significant bilateral conversations. Our Prime Minister is bound to be meeting each of the visiting heads of state and government who seeks a meeting. And that may mean a dozen important meetings with these country leaders. And for us, of course, both the meeting with President Xi and the meeting with President Putin are going to grab world headlines," the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP said.Former Union minister Salman Khurshid also described the gathering as a “significant event” that allows India to demonstrate leadership on the global stage.Speaking to ANI, Khurshid stressed that the presence of leaders from all 11 member countries, including China, Iran, Russia, South Africa and India, could help New Delhi bring countries together, reduce contradictions and conflicts, and work towards creating better conditions in the world."This is a significant event. We hosted the G20 summit a few years ago, and the important thing is that the top leadership of China, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and India will all be present. All 11 countries will be present. It allows India to demonstrate leadership and ensure that contradictions and conflicts are reduced to a minimum. It can't be done overnight, but at least some attempt should be made. For India to have a locus as the leader and chairperson of the Brics summit, to be able to bring people together, converge, and accept positions that will create better conditions in the world," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said leaders from across the world would gather in New Delhi over the next few days for the Brics summit, expressing confidence that the high-level meeting would see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind.“Over the next few days, leaders from around the world will gather for the Brics Summit. I am confident that the Summit will see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind,” Modi said in a post on X in Hindi.The Prime Minister also shared a Sanskrit shlok highlighting the importance of cultivating relationships with virtuous people and promoting dialogue and goodwill.“A person should always live among the virtuous and cultivate their company. A person should engage in discussion and foster friendly relations with the virtuous, because mutual goodwill, dialogue and friendly relations strengthen peace and cooperation,” the verse said in a loose translation.As Brics chair in 2026, India will host the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of Brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.During the summit, leaders are expected to discuss ways to strengthen intra-Brics cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.Earlier on Thursday night, Bharat Mandapam, the venue for the summit in New Delhi, was being readied to host the high-profile gathering, with leaders and representatives from across the world expected to arrive for the September 12-13 event.

Article Title: Brics hammers out joint declaration after India bridges Iran-UAE chasm
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a dramatic repeat of the 2023 G20 Declaration under India’s presidency, Brics member-states reached a consensus for a joint declaration following intensive, late-night negotiations that lasted till 4 am on Saturday. The talks had been strained by sharp differences between the UAE and Iran over the West Asia conflict and an earlier meeting of the Brics foreign ministers under India’s presidency had ended without a consensual statement.The 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration announced by PM Narendra Modi was solidified by a rare leader-level Iran-UAE meeting - between Iran President Masour Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan – in the middle of the war that started on February 28.In a delicately worded compromise, the declaration addressed the interests of both sides by expressing serious concerns over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and also peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), in violation of international law and relevant resolutions of the IAEA. This implicit criticism of US-Israeli action against Iran was crucial in getting Iran to sign off on the declaration.“We in Brics must fight against the normalization of attacks on civilian, vital infrastructure. The same applies to peaceful nuclear infrastructure," said Pezeshkian at the summit​​​.Nuclear safeguards, safety, and security must always be upheld, including in armed conflicts, to protect people and the environment from harm, said the declaration.Significantly, the joint statement did not name any country or explicitly condemn attacks, prioritising instead dialogue and diplomacy, UN Charter, civilian lives and infrastructure and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States, while also expressing deep concern over continued escalations and calling for maximum restraint.In the declaration, the leaders recalled their respective national positions on West Asia and stressed the need to work together to maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law.Official sources said India led prolonged negotiations at multiple levels to reconcile sharp differences between the 2 sides and forge consensus with support from other member-states who were keen that the summit didn’t end without a joint statement.The Brics consensus is reminiscent of the last-minute G20 2023 Delhi declaration that was achieved in the middle of the escalating Russia-Ukraine war with a carefully nuanced formulation that called upon all States to refrain from use of force for territorial acquisition but without naming Russia.The Brics declaration also came days before Iran’s meeting with GCC countries on the Strait of Hormuz situation. In Pezeshkian’s meeting with the crown prince, the leaders underscored the importance of supporting efforts to ease tensions, promote de-escalation and strengthen regional stability.Indian officials had on Friday expressed confidence about a constructive outcome from the negotiations, following Modi’s meeting with Pezeshkian in which he expressed solidarity with Tehran, seeking a long-term and win-win partnership with Iran.On other issues, like in Rio last year, China and Russia, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, reiterated their support to the aspirations of Brazil and India to play a greater role in the UN, including the Security Council.Importantly for India, the declaration expressed strong condemnation of any acts of terrorism as “criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation, whenever, wherever and by whomsoever committed” and strongly reiterated condemnation of the Pahalgam terrorist attack.“We reaffirm our commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens,” said the declaration.On the Palestine issue, Brics countries, including India, expressed deep concern on the continued violence in Gaza despite the ceasefire agreement of October 2025. “We call for halting any policies aimed at forced displacement of Palestinians from Gaza Strip and express concern regarding arrangements that may prejudice the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and legitimize or prolong occupation,” said the declaration.There was no mention of the Ukraine war in the declaration this year. The declaration backed comprehensive reform of the UN, including the Security Council, with a view to making it more “democratic, representative, effective and efficient” and to increase the representation of developing countries in the Council's memberships.
Article Summary: The 140-paragraph new delhi declaration announced by pm narendra modi was solidified by a rare leader-level iran-uae meeting. The talks had been strained by sharp differences between the uae and iran over the west asia conflict. In a delicately worded compromise, the declaration addressed the interests of both sides.

Article Title: Thaw in ties deserves to be cherished, says Xi; border peace is essential: PM Modi
Article Text:
The two sides look to reinforce the thaw in relationship with another meeting between the leaders.

NEW DELHI: Chinese President Xi Jinping told PM Narendra Modi the current momentum in bilateral ties anchored in resumption of institutional exchanges, expanding cooperation agenda and increasing trade is hard-won and deserves to be cherished, as both sides looked to reinforce the thaw in the relationship with another meeting between the leaders.While PM Modi joined Xi in welcoming the “steady progress” in bilateral relations, he underlined India’s position that peace and tranquility in border areas will act as an essential basis for continued development of the relationship.The leaders met on the margins of the BRICS summit for what was their third bilateral meeting in 2 years, starting with Kazan in 2024 and Tianjin last year. In their 40-minute meeting, the first on Indian soil in 7 years, PM Modi and Xi agreed that both countries should take a strategic and long-term perspective of their ties and differences should not cause disputes.Xi reiterated India and China are partners, not rivals, but the Indian readout on this occasion, unlike the Tianjin statement by India last year, skipped mention of that formulation.PM Modi also underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues. An Indian readout said they expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question proceeding from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two peoples.The PM also raised the issue of India’s trade deficit with China and the need for supply chain predictability. According to the Indian side, they underlined the need to address each other’s concerns, including structural trade imbalance and supply chain issues, and facilitation of meaningful and predictable market access.Since their meeting in Kazan in 2024, which marked the end of the eastern Ladakh border standoff, three rounds of Special Representatives talks on the boundary question have taken place. In the last meeting, they agreed to advance negotiations for an early and substantial harvest of boundary delimitation and border management.PM Modi and Xi noted the progress in people-to-people ties and underscored the need to further promote cultural exchanges, business linkages and greater mobility between the two countries, said the Indian side. “Prime Minister highlighted that both sides must be guided by three mutuals- mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest,” said the readout, adding that they agreed to expand common ground on regional and global issues, and in addressing challenges.In his remarks, Xi proposed more rational strategic assessment of the relationship looking forward, win-win cooperation, mutual respect and understanding and inclusive multilateral cooperation.A Chinese readout of the meeting quoted PM Modi as saying that India follows an independent foreign policy and its ties with Beijing are not influenced by any third country. It also said that Modi told Xi India’s position on Taiwan and Tibet-related issues have not changed and it will not allow anyone to carry out anti-China activities.The Chinese foreign ministry had attributed the same remark to external affairs minister S Jaishankar after his meeting with counterpart Wang Yi in July this year. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) had responded by saying that while India had never violated China’s sovereignty, China was in illegal occupation of Indian territory in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh since 1963.
Article Summary: The leaders met on the margins of the brics summit for what was their third bilateral meeting in 2 years. In their 40-minute meeting, the first on indian soil in 7 years, pm modi and xi agreed that both countries should take a strategic and long-term perspective of ties.

Article Title: Modi: Global South must shape, not just follow, rules
Article Text:
These should be focused on representation, responsiveness and rulemaking, PM Modi said.

Modi positions Brics as an inclusive, not anti-west, forum

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Declaring the 18th Brics leaders' summit open, PM Narendra Modi stressed that UN Security Council (UNSC) reforms cannot be delayed any longer and that the "pyramid of privilege" reflected in the current global governance structure must be transformed into a "platform of partnership".Modi focused on economic integration of the Global South in his address at the session on inclusive governance and multilateralism, saying the bloc must work together to turn developing countries from rule-takers to rule-shapers."The Global South today stands in the front row of global crises, but in the back row of decision-making," the PM said, proposing that Brics draft 10 proposals for global governance reform.These should be focused on representation, responsiveness and rulemaking, PM Modi said. He sought a system “where every country has a voice, every member has a stake and the development of humanity remains at the centre of all endeavours”.Also read | Brics hammers out joint declaration after India bridges Iran-UAE chasm On representation, he said UNSC reform can no longer be delayed and text-based negotiations on this subject must be tied to a fixed timeline and clear outcomes. “Similarly, voting power, leadership positions and policy priorities within global financial institutions must reflect today’s economic realities.Countries driving global economic growth deserve an appropriate role in shaping global economic governance,” he added.While western experts have often described Brics as an anti-West forum, Modi said the grouping operates not against anyone, but with an inclusive approach that brings everyone along. “Today, Brics is also in its coming-of-age moment. Over the past 20 years, Brics has established a distinct identity on the global stage. We respect each other’s perspectives and move forward through consensus,” he said.The PM called upon the bloc to work on an ambitious new agenda, translating its unity and consensus into concrete results on the global stage. He proposed establishment of a Brics Continuity and Implementation Mechanism. “Brics presidency changes every year, but this should not disrupt our institutional momentum. Under this mechanism, all initiatives and outcomes can be followed up through the troika (past, current and incoming presidency),” said Modi.Also read | UN hails Iran-UAE meeting on sidelines of Brics Summit, says India can be 'bridge-builder' Raising the issue of seafarers’ safety, Modi talked about how they make a massive contribution to global trade and yet lack adequate support in difficult times. He proposed creating a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to connect maritime authorities and missions of relevant nations. “This network would assist with distress alerts, medical aid, family notifications and evacuation efforts.”He said ensuring equal participation in setting the global rules of the future is critical. “AI, cyberspace, outer space, biotechnology and critical technologies are shaping not only future opportunities, but also future rules. We must work to transform the Global South from rule-takers to rule-shapers,” he said. “The message of this Brics summit must be clear: if our future is shared, the right to shape it must also be shared,” he said.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi positions brics as an inclusive, not anti-west, forum. He proposes that brics draft 10 proposals for global governance reform. These should be focused on representation, responsiveness and rulemaking, pm modi said. He sought a system “where every country has a voice, every member has a stake”

Article Title: Gucchi marmik, millet pulao, khumb galouti: What's on the Brics gala dinner menu
Article Text:
Brics gala dinner menu showcases an all-vegetarian Indian spread

What’s on the dinner menu

‘Brics Symphony’ at gala dinner

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's gala dinner for Brics leaders and other visiting dignitaries is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on Saturday evening, following the first day of the Brics Summit. The dinner is expected to conclude in the next 10 to 15 minutes.The evening features a specially curated Indian menu showcasing regional flavours and traditional preparations, along with a cultural performance by an ensemble of more than 100 artistes from India and other Brics member countries.The gala dinner features a specially curated Indian menu that brings together regional flavours, traditional recipes and contemporary interpretations of Indian cuisine.The meal begins with Khandvi Mille - Feuille, a steamed gram-flour roll tempered with mustard, coconut and curry leaves, served with Kesar mango, micro-greens and yoghurt dressing. The starters also include Khumb Galouti, tender pan-grilled mushroom kebabs with mint pearls, served on a bed of sheermal bread.The main course features Paneer Lababdar, soft cottage cheese cubes simmered in a rich gravy of shallots and tomato, alongside Gucchi Marmik, Himalayan morel mushrooms and tender asparagus gently simmered with saffron, raisins and mamra almonds.Other dishes on the menu include Carrot Bean Poriyal, made with carrots and green beans toasted in aromatic South Indian spices in hand-pressed virgin coconut oil and finished with freshly grated coconut. Thakkali Belle Saaru, a light lentil broth of toor dal enriched with fresh tomatoes and curry leaves, is also being served, along with Millet Pulao, Beetroot Raita and assorted Indian breads.The dessert selection includes Old Delhi Fruit Cream with Jalebi, pairing seasonal fruits and lightly whipped cream with a crispy sweet fritter, and Shahtoot Phirni, a slow-cooked pudding of milk and rice topped with sweet mulberries and gold leaf.The dinner is being accompanied by ‘Brics Symphony’, a cultural performance featuring an ensemble of around 160 artistes, with Indian dancers and musicians forming the core of the troupe.Indian artistes are performing classical dance forms including Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi and Kathak, representing different regions of the country. Traditional Indian instruments are also being featured alongside musicians from other Brics member countries.The performance, being coordinated by the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), is expected to run for around 20 to 25 minutes and will include intermittent vocal renditions.Dinner follows packed first summit dayThe gala dinner comes after a busy opening day of the BRICS Summit, which brought together Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and other world leaders and senior dignitaries in New Delhi.A New Delhi Declaration was adopted at the end of the first day of the summit. PM Modi also unveiled a 10-point roadmap for global governance reform under the BRICS framework and called for a ‘Seafarers' Emergency Support Network’ to protect sailors facing heightened risks from global and regional crises.Earlier on Saturday, PM Modi and visiting leaders also visited the Bharat Innovates Exhibition at the Bharat Mandapam complex and participated in a tree-planting programme on the lawns of the convention centre.India assumed its fourth Brics chairship on January 1, 2026, with the chairship guided by the theme ‘Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability’. The year also marks 20 years since the establishment of BRICS.

NEW DELHI: India hosted the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together leaders of the expanded 11-member grouping for discussions on global conflicts, terrorism , trade, energy, technology, climate change and reform of international institutions. India used its 2026 chairship to push a people-centric agenda centred on resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability.The summit was marked by high-level bilateral meetings, visible displays of bonhomie among leaders and efforts to bridge differences over the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region. PM Modi held separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, while leaders also participated in the Brics Business Forum and other summit engagements.From PM Modi and Putin travelling together by car inside the Bharat Mandapam complex to PM Modi and Xi sharing warm moments and the leaders participating in a gala dinner and cultural engagements, the summit combined diplomacy with symbols of Brics unity.Also read - 'Global South must be rule-shaper, India ready to take lead': PM Modi at Brics Summit The summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration, a 45-page document containing 140 points that brings together the grouping's positions on terrorism, unilateral military action, West Asia, global governance, trade, sanctions, energy, finance and development.PM Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the summit, with both sides stressing the importance of viewing India-China relations from a strategic and long-term perspective.The two leaders committed to seeking a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution to the boundary question. PM Modi stressed that differences should not become disputes and highlighted the importance of mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest.The discussions also covered peace and tranquillity along the border, economic relations, trade imbalances, supply chains and people-to-people exchanges. The meeting came as New Delhi and Beijing seek to stabilise bilateral ties while continuing to manage differences over the boundary.The Modi-Xi meeting was one of the summit's most closely watched engagements, given the strategic importance of India-China relations and their simultaneous participation in an expanded Brics framework.PM Modi held an over 45-minute bilateral meeting with Putin on the eve of the summit, reviewing the India-Russia strategic partnership and discussing regional and global developments.The two leaders discussed the impact of the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the West Asia crisis on maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers. PM Modi reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy remained the way forward in resolving conflicts and said India was ready to contribute to peace efforts.Five Indian seafarers have died in the Black Sea amid the Russia-Ukraine hostilities, making maritime safety an important concern for New Delhi.The two sides also discussed defence, energy, critical minerals, civil nuclear cooperation, fertilisers, infrastructure, technology and industrial cooperation. India and Russia agreed to work towards taking bilateral trade to $100 billion by 2030.Putin also invited PM Modi to Russia for the 24th India-Russia Annual Summit. The dates will be finalised through diplomatic channels.After their bilateral meeting, PM Modi and Putin travelled together in the same car inside the Bharat Mandapam complex before attending the Brics Business Forum.The unusual visual quickly became one of the defining moments of the summit, highlighting the close nature of the India-Russia relationship amid continuing geopolitical pressure on Moscow and India's effort to maintain strategic autonomy.PM Modi later highlighted the growing India-Russia economic relationship, including the participation of companies from both countries at the INNOPROM industrial exhibition held at Bharat Mandapam.PM Modi presented Putin with a Russian translation of the Thirukkural, the classical Tamil work attributed to poet-saint Thiruvalluvar."Two thousand years ago, Thiruvalluvar wrote the Thirukkural. It includes the entire gamut of human life. It has been translated into the Russian language. I am confident that the people-to-people contact will increase with the translation of the Thirukkural into Russian, which will play a big role in strengthening our relations," Modi told Putin.The gift was presented as a cultural bridge between India and Russia and reflected the emphasis placed by India on people-to-people links during its Brics chairship.PM Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the summit, with the two leaders discussing India-Iran relations, Brics cooperation and the conflict in West Asia.PM Modi reiterated India's position that disputes must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy and stressed the need for lasting peace and stability in the region.The discussions also covered freedom of navigation and commerce and the safety and well-being of seafarers, issues that have acquired greater importance amid disruption to shipping routes in the region.The meeting followed the leaders' earlier interaction on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. India also stressed the importance of expanding bilateral trade channels and pursuing a long-term and mutually beneficial relationship with Iran.The summit was accompanied by a series of high-profile visuals showing leaders of the expanded grouping interacting informally.PM Modi was seen greeting Putin and Xi together, holding their hands and sharing smiles. In another visual, Modi walked alongside Putin, Xi and Pezeshkian.Also read - Big reunion at Brics: PM Modi, Xi & Putin meet for 3rd time in 3 yrs; PM shares photo PM Modi was also seen holding hands and walking alongside Pezeshkian and other leaders during the Brics Business Forum. The images were widely seen as a demonstration of the grouping's effort to project unity despite differences among members on major geopolitical issues.The presence of leaders from Russia, China, Iran, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, South Africa and other member states underscored the diversity of interests represented within the expanded grouping.The Brics leaders also attended a gala dinner hosted during the summit, providing an informal setting for interactions between heads of government and state.Also read - Gucchi marmik, millet pulao, khumb galouti: What's on the Brics gala dinner menu The cultural programme and dinner formed part of India's effort to showcase its heritage alongside the formal diplomatic agenda. The event brought together leaders who had spent the summit discussing contentious issues ranging from wars and terrorism to trade and global governance.The informal interactions added a softer dimension to a summit otherwise dominated by difficult geopolitical negotiations.A symbolic tree plantation ceremony was also organised during the summit, with Brics leaders participating in the planting of a Banyan tree.The Banyan tree, known for its extensive roots and interconnected branches, was presented as a symbol of continuity, resilience and interconnectedness. The gesture complemented India's 2026 Brics theme of "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability".Also read - PM Modi, Brics leaders take part in joint tree plantation at Bharat Mandapam: Watch The plantation also reflected India's attempt to connect the summit's diplomatic agenda with sustainability and environmental cooperation.The Brics Business Forum brought together heads of state, ministers and business leaders to discuss trade, investment, finance, technology and development.PM Modi highlighted the economic weight of the expanded grouping, saying:"Today, BRICS nations represent 50 per cent of the world's population, 40 per cent of its GDP, and over 25 per cent of global trade. Moreover, while global GDP has grown approximately two-and-a-half-fold over these years, the combined GDP of BRICS nations has expanded nearly four-and-a-half-fold. In other words, the economic strength of BRICS has grown at nearly twice the pace of the rest of the world.""The growing scale, speed, and optimism of BRICS are clearly evident among us. This forum, hosted in India, is the largest BRICS Business Forum to date," the Prime Minister added.Also read - Brics New Delhi Declaration adopted: Terrorism, conflict resolution, tariff concerns addressed; key points Pezeshkian called for Brics to convert its economic potential into practical cooperation through trade, investment and joint financing."We believe that the true strength of BRICS is not confined merely to the size of its members' economies; rather, it becomes more apparent when these capacities are transformed into a network of trade, investment and joint financing – a transition from potential cooperation to operational one," he said.Putin stressed the importance of business-to-business relations and economic partnerships, arguing that they could help create more resilient international economic relations.At the Business Forum, Putin criticised what he described as attempts by Western competitors to regain their former economic leadership."We have always been told that competition is a sacred cow, something that must not be touched," Putin told a BRICS business forum event. "Yet, unfortunately, ​today your Western competitors are trying by any means necessary to regain their former leadership.""This ⁠competition is ‌sometimes assuming unsightly forms," he said. "They even include direct ​physical attacks or the ​destruction of industrial and logistical facilities, pipelines, and so forth."Putin also criticised restrictions on international transport corridors, shipping and trade and called for Brics to contribute to building "a new, sustainable platform for global growth".The summit also provided an opportunity for India and Russia to discuss expanding economic cooperation amid Western sanctions and geopolitical uncertainty.The two countries discussed the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030 and cooperation in infrastructure, energy, technology, defence, critical minerals and civil nuclear energy.The sides also explored industrial cooperation in railways and tunnelling, the steel value chain and greater access to the Russian market for Indian exporters.India continues to maintain strong energy ties with Russia, while seeking to expand trade beyond traditional sectors.India's 2026 chairship focused heavily on converting Brics into a platform for practical cooperation rather than limiting it to political declarations.More than 350 meetings and high-level engagements were organised across approximately 30 cities during India's chairship. These covered political and security cooperation, economic and financial cooperation, and cultural and people-to-people exchanges.PM Modi said: "It gives me immense pleasure to welcome and greet you all to India. India’s BRICS chairmanship is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach. Resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability have been our priorities.""Alongside these priorities, we have placed special emphasis on connecting BRICS cooperation with the common people. With this vision in mind, more than 350 meetings were organised. We had the opportunity to welcome your teams to approximately 30 cities..."Brics countries agreed on new mechanisms to strengthen agricultural cooperation.These include Centres of Excellence on agro-ecology for research and knowledge sharing on natural, organic and regenerative farming, a Brics Network on Digital Agriculture using artificial intelligence, geospatial intelligence, IoT-enabled monitoring and advanced data analytics, and BRICS AGRIN, a voluntary framework covering agricultural inputs, seeds and genetic resources.The initiatives seek to promote climate-resilient farming and greater technology-driven cooperation among member countries.The Brics Mission for Healthy Lifestyle was launched along with a roadmap for joint cooperation for 2026-2029, focusing on preventive approaches to obesity and other non-communicable diseases.Members also agreed to establish an Expert Working Group on Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine, covering research, evidence generation, academic exchange, quality standards and protection of traditional knowledge.Mental health cooperation was also strengthened through the Brics Training Hub Network and Network of Centres of Excellence, with NIMHANS India as the coordinating centre.Brics adopted guiding principles on energy storage and smart grids and launched a Digital Centre of Excellence for Smart Grids and Energy Storage.The initiative will provide a platform for knowledge sharing, capacity building, policy and regulatory cooperation and pilot projects among member countries.The summit also placed emphasis on energy security, diversified energy sources and equitable energy transitions.India pushed stronger cooperation for micro, small and medium enterprises and startups.The Brics MSME Cooperation Portal will connect MSMEs, technology centres, trade associations, financial institutions and policymakers across member countries.A Brics Incubator Network will connect startups with incubators in other member countries, while the Brics Startup Innovation Fund is intended to support early and growth-stage startups.Brics members agreed on a Logistics Supply-Chain Cooperation Framework aimed at improving resilience, sustainability and connectivity.The grouping also advanced cooperation on global value chains through the GVC Action Plan 2026-2030, including a Technical Council and joint study.The initiatives are intended to reduce vulnerabilities caused by fragmented supply chains, improve connectivity and promote economic diversification.The summit also advanced cooperation on sustainable urban development.A Brics Urban Mobility Hub was established as a platform for technical cooperation and knowledge sharing. Members also adopted voluntary principles on climate-resilient urban infrastructure.An Urban Research and Knowledge Network was established to facilitate cross-border research, peer learning and institutional cooperation.India also advanced cooperation on skills and employment through BRICS CONNECT, a voluntary network covering capacity building, social security, women's workforce participation, employability and digital public infrastructure.The Brics Youth Cooperation Framework 2026 was adopted to provide greater continuity and structure to youth cooperation.Sports technology cooperation was institutionalised through a working group focusing on technical information, research, institutional experience and best practices.The Brics Science and Research Repository was welcomed as a structured platform for sharing scientific knowledge among member countries.The initiative is intended to strengthen research collaboration and facilitate greater exchange of scientific information across the expanded grouping.Brics currently comprises 11 countries: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the UAE.The expansion has significantly widened the grouping's geographical reach across Asia, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America. It has also brought together countries with different political systems, economic priorities and positions on major international conflicts.India's chairship therefore focused not only on expanding cooperation but also on finding consensus among members with competing interests.The summit concluded with the adoption of the New Delhi Declaration 2026, following intensive negotiations among members. The 45-page declaration contains 140 points and represents India's central diplomatic outcome from its 2026 chairship.The declaration addresses terrorism, conflicts, global governance, trade, sanctions, energy, finance, development and the interests of the Global South.The declaration strongly condemns terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and calls for "zero tolerance for terrorism".It specifically condemns the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terrorist attack, in which 26 people were killed. The declaration also condemns cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens.Brics reaffirmed that terrorism cannot be associated with any religion, nationality, civilisation or ethnic group and called for those involved in terrorist activities and their support to be held accountable.The grouping also called for progress towards the adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism under the UN framework.The declaration expresses deep concern over the continuing escalation in West Asia and calls on all parties to exercise maximum restraint.It stresses dialogue, consultation and diplomacy as the means to address conflicts and calls for the protection of civilians and humanitarian assistance.On Gaza, Brics called for the upholding of a ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian aid and an end to forced displacement of Palestinians. It reaffirmed support for a two-state solution based on the internationally recognised 1967 borders.The declaration condemns unilateral military action without naming any country.The language assumes significance because Brics includes members with differing positions on the major conflicts in West Asia and the wider international system.The consensus was reached after negotiations continued into the early hours of Saturday, with India working to bridge differences between members and produce a common position.Brics reaffirmed its support for comprehensive reform of the United Nations, including the Security Council.The grouping called for greater representation of developing countries in global decision-making and a more democratic, representative and inclusive international system.China and Russia reiterated support for the aspirations of India and Brazil to play a greater role in the UN, including the Security Council.The declaration expresses concern over unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that distort international trade and create uncertainty for businesses and supply chains.Brics reaffirmed support for a rules-based multilateral trading system centred on the World Trade Organization.The grouping also called for the restoration of a fully functioning two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism.Brics voiced opposition to unilateral coercive measures that it considers inconsistent with international law and the principles of the UN Charter.The declaration calls for such measures to be eliminated and highlights their impact on international economic relations.The position reflects a longstanding Brics push for a more balanced international economic and political order.The declaration supports greater use of local currencies in cross-border payments and trade settlements among Brics countries.Members acknowledged ongoing work on interoperability between payment and messaging systems and efforts to facilitate trade settlements and investment in local currencies.The initiative forms part of the wider Brics effort to strengthen financial resilience and cooperation.The declaration calls for stronger energy security through diversified energy sources, resilient infrastructure and stable markets.It also supports just, orderly, equitable and inclusive energy transitions while recognising the differing circumstances and priorities of member countries.Brics backed cooperation involving renewables, nuclear energy, hydropower, hydrogen, fossil fuels and other low-carbon technologies.The declaration recognises women as leaders, decision-makers and drivers of economic growth and social transformation.It highlights women's participation in governance, entrepreneurship, employment and peacebuilding and calls for greater financial and digital inclusion.The grouping also emphasised skills development and access to productive and social services.Brics expressed concern over illicit financial flows linked to drug trafficking, firearms trafficking, terrorism financing, human trafficking and organised crime.The grouping called for stronger cooperation between member countries to trace and disrupt criminal proceeds and tackle transnational criminal networks.The New Delhi Declaration combines a strong political message on terrorism, unilateral military action, West Asia and global governance with a broad economic and development agenda.For India, the outcome represents an effort to demonstrate that the expanded Brics can reach consensus despite major geopolitical differences. Article Title: Brics opposes unilateral trade steps like EU carbon border tax
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Brics nations Saturday opposed unilateral trade measures such as EU’s carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), saying such measures undermine efforts by developing countries aimed at addressing the adverse impacts of climate change.Though they recognised the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to meet climate goals, the grouping’s members sought to delink any unilateral punitive action from achieving a common goal and pitched for energy security for all based on a pragmatic approach where “fossil fuel”, they said, will still play an important role in the world’s energy mix”, particularly for emerging markets and developing economies, in addition to renewable sources and nuclear.CBAM, which entered its operational regime on Jan 1, is a tool to put a price, through imposing a border tax, on carbon-intensive goods, like iron and steel, aluminium and cement, that are entering the 27 EU nations.Though BRICS nations opposed the proposal from the time it was conceived, arguing that the unilateral move placed an additional burden on businesses in developing economies due to embedded emissions in their products, they made their points a part of New Delhi Declaration calling it “punitive, discriminatory and protectionist measures that are not in line with international law”.Without any attempt to dilute their respective efforts to meet climate action goals under the Paris Agreement, the nations called for greater actions based on equity and the UN’s principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities, in light of different national circumstances.They also highlighted the need to enhance energy security by ensuring energy market stability and maintaining undisrupted flows of energy from diverse sources including fossil fuels. Incidentally, four of the BRICS group countries such as Russia, Saudi Arabia, Iran and UAE are among the major global exporters of fossil fuel.Sending a positive signal ahead of COP31, scheduled to take place in Turkey in Nov, they called on all countries to uphold their commitment to maintain and scale up efforts to combat climate change, and expressed their confidence in multilateralism to address the global challenge.
Article Summary: Brics nations saturday opposed unilateral trade measures such as eu’s carbon border adjustment mechanism (cbam) they said such measures undermine efforts by developing countries aimed at addressing the adverse impacts of climate change. Cbam is a tool to put a price, through imposing a border tax, on carbon-intensive goods.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India's success against the odds in bringing Brics countries with incongruent, even conflicting, outlooks on key global issues of contention, such as the West Asia conflict, to throw their weight behind a joint declaration comes as a timely domestic boost for BJP when its rivals are sensing some vulnerability in its otherwise dominant political position.Foreign policy has been a major component of BJP's arsenal in scoring political points over its rivals, especially Congress, as it has projected a rising global profile of an assertive India under PM Narendra Modi 's leadership, in contrast to the country's "meek" response to challenges from external security to trade in the pre-2014 period.Modi hailed the New Delhi Declaration, adopted unanimously at Brics, saying confidence of the bloc is wider in reach and stronger in purpose.With BJP marshalling a counter-offensive against the opposition and set to step up its public connect with a month-long campaign from Modi's birthday (Sept 17), the Brics outcome will be one more arrow in its quiver. The photograph of Modi holding the hand of Iran's President Masoud and leading him into Bharat Mandapam, the fact that Indian diplomacy was crucial in getting Iran and its rival the UAE to sign the declaration as well as the tough formulation against coercive tariff and unilateral sanctions can only blunt opposition's criticism about diminished strategic autonomy because of pressure from US.That the resolution did not mention US by name does not take away much from the perception of India holding its own at the summit which the Trump administration must have been watching closely.All this is a perfect fit for Modi's "strong leader" brand.The G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration in 2023, with a gulf separating Russia and the West over invasion of Ukraine too, had come amid a cloud of uncertainty over such a possibility. Working with others, India somehow conjured up a document that was unanimously adopted. The diplomatic success became a major talking point for NDA in the run-up to the 2024 elections.A similar success at Brics attests to the governing alliance's contention that India now enjoys a standing that can persuade global leaders to get around their differences to thrash out a consensus outcome.In his post on X on the declaration, Modi said with the document's focus on innovation, sustainability, people-to-people ties and more, the endeavour is to make cooperation practical, development-oriented and responsive to the aspirations of Brics nations.BJP was quick to drive home its message. Its president Nitin Nabin said Bharat has once again demonstrated its commitment to a more representative and balanced world.

New Delhi: PM Narendra Modi met his Malaysian and Ethiopian counterparts, Anwar Ibrahim and Abiy Ahm-ed Ali, on the sidelines of the Brics summit Saturday. Officials said the meetings took relations with both countries on a new trajectory, as Malaysia and Ethiopia expressed keenness for stronger defence cooperation with India.Joint personnel training as well as defence procurem-ent from India was discussed, according to officials. Both countries welcomed Indian industry and investment.Ethiopia welcomed Indian mining companies. "Opportunities in the semiconductor industry were discussed with Malaysia," said a source. Malaysia also agreed to the opening of a new Indian consulate in the country.According to an official readout, Modi and Ibrahim took stock of the outcomes of the former's visit to Malaysia in Feb and reviewed progress in bilateral cooperation acro-ss a range of areas, including trade and investment, defence and security, semiconductors, infrastructure, digital economy, energy, fintech, education, tourism and people-to-people ties. Ibrahim conveyed Malaysia's concurrence to the establishment of a consulate general of India in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah."PM Modi appreciated Malaysia's continued support in strengthening Asean-India relations. The leaders exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest. They expressed their continued commitment to advancing the India-Malaysia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," said the Indian readout.The meeting with the Ethiopian PM saw the leaders discussing strengthening of the bilateral strategic partnership. They reviewed progress across sectors like economic cooperation, defence and security partnership, and capacity building. It built on Modi's visit to Addis Ababa in Dec 2025, said an Indian readout. They reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation in multilateral forums, according to officials."PM Narendra Modi noted that (Ethiopia's) presence helped in reinforcing the collective voice of the Global South," said the readout.
